description: Discovery hypothesis: billing staff may need to reconcile claim-level and provider-level adjustments against expected payments. The workflow is documented, but a remaining software gap among small practices is not.
customer_segment: Hypothesized segment: small US professional practices receiving Medicare remittance advice; not all healthcare payers.
context: Post-adjudication billing/accounting work, distinct from the pre-service authorization problem. No claims or personal data accessed.

evidence.text: CMS describes remittances spanning multiple claims and adjustments at line, claim and provider levels.
CMS states that ERA can automatically post amounts and adjustments to billing/accounting applications rather than manual staff posting from paper.

alternatives: Electronic remittance advice integrated with accounting/billing applications.
CMS identifies free Medicare Easy Print for professional providers and PC Print for institutional providers; these are not claimed to perform every reconciliation task.

contradictory_evidence.text: CMS already describes standardized electronic remittance and automatic posting, weakening the case for a generic replacement of manual entry.
CMS identifies free remittance viewing/printing tools, so displaying or explaining codes alone is not demonstrated differentiation.

uncertainty: No measured exception frequency, manual-posting prevalence, small-practice dissatisfaction, buyer budget, or unmet reconciliation requirement. Existing standardized tools may adequately solve much of the work.
open_questions: Which exceptions remain unresolved after a practice already uses ERA auto-posting?
Are those exceptions frequent enough and economically meaningful enough to justify a separate tool?
next_actions: Prioritize evidence of specific unresolved exceptions over generic payment-automation claims.
Pause deeper work if available billing systems already handle the identified exceptions.
title: Posting and explaining Medicare payment adjustments in small practices

history.reason: Initial public-source discovery for issue #4; no customer interviews or commercial validation.
